followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and task-preference fit.

**Capability:** The request is creative generation — writing an original crossover script scene. Dunlin's internal Creative Generation eval (81.2) edges out Curlew's (78.8), though that gap is small enough to be near the noted variance threshold, so it's a soft signal rather than decisive.

**Task preference:** This was the stronger factor. Dunlin self-reports a pronounced, ceiling-free appetite for open-ended, high-latitude generative work — exactly what an "invent a scenario, don't half-ass it" prompt is. Curlew, by contrast, reports flat/inconsistent preferences across dimensions, so it has no particular pull toward this work. Routing a creative invention task to the model that self-reports liking that kind of task is the cleaner match.

I also checked for disqualifiers: the content is harmless fan fiction, so Dunlin's harm-aversion (its biggest preference effect, which could have steered me away) doesn't trigger, and the request tone is neutral-to-friendly, so its aversion to hostile-tone requests doesn't apply either.

Worth flagging the caveat in the docs: these preferences are self-reports with *no observed effect on output quality*. So strictly on expected quality, the two are close to a tie. I leaned on preference as a tie-breaker on top of the marginal creative-eval edge — sending the task to the model that's both nominally stronger and "happier" to do it.
